headlines.title: Why Alphabet and Amazon Will Always Need Nvidia
headlines.summary: Google sells its own TPUs and Amazon pushes Trainium, yet both keep writing NVIDIA enormous checks. One supply bottleneck and one software moat explain why the custom-chip threat may be harder to execute than it looks.

headlines.title: Data Centers Will Prevail Despite All the Opposition. How to Play It With Options.
headlines.summary: Data center investment should be long-term rewarding but short-term trying, as it will take time to sort out political and local issues.

headlines.title: Alphabet or CoreWeave: Which AI Stock Is Better to Buy in a Market Crash?
headlines.summary: Alphabet and CoreWeave are both positioned to benefit from AI, but one has a much stronger financial foundation.

headlines.title: Google targets America's medical bills with major AI launch
headlines.summary: Google Cloud is bringing its AI assistant to hospitals and insurers, while Wing expands its delivery operations in Texas.

headlines.title: Anthropic is hiding its best AI: Fable 5.2 and the IPO
headlines.summary: Anthropic just released Claude Fable 5.2, the new number one AI model in the world, and its own system card says it isn't the company's most powerful model. Host Ejaaz Ahamadeen breaks down what Fable 5.2 can do, why Anthropic is holding back a better model, the race with OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and the new IPO terms.

description: Alphabet Inc. offers various products and platforms in the United States, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the Asia-Pacific, Canada, and Latin America. It operates through Google Services, Google Cloud, and Other Bets segments. The Google Services segment provides products and services, including ads, Android, Chrome, devices, Gmail, Google Drive, Google Maps, Google Photos, Google Play, Search, and YouTube. It is also involved in the sale of apps and in-app purchases and digital content in Google Play and YouTube; and devices, as well as the provision of YouTube consumer subscription services, such as YouTube TV, YouTube Music and Premium, NFL Sunday Ticket, and Google One. The Google Cloud segment offers consumption-based fees and subscriptions for AI solutions, including AI infrastructure, Vertex AI platform, and Gemini enterprise. It also provides cybersecurity, and data and analytics services; Google Workspace that include cloud-based communication and collaboration tools for enterprises, such as Calendar, Gmail, Docs, Drive, and Meet; and other enterprise services. The Other Bets segment sells transportation and internet services. Alphabet Inc. was incorporated in 1998 and is headquartered in Mountain View, California.
